cohort: The study included 28,998,245 hospital births in Brazil from 2012 to 2022.
finding: Marked racial disparities were found in cesarean rates in Brazil, with White women having the highest rates and Indigenous women the lowest.
mod_finding: Overall, 56.44% of deliveries were cesarean, with rates highest among White women (66.66%) and lowest among Indigenous women (21.23%), and Robson Group 5 being the most prevalent and contributing most to cesarean rates across all racial groups.
